About 3 months ago, our 3-month-old puppy Mylo swallowed a large mutton bone from the trash. An initial X-ray at another hospital showed it was stuck in his throat near the neck. He was vomiting and not eating anything, and as time passed, he started breathing strangely, almost as if he was choking. We were extremely worried.

Through a common friend, we connected with Dr. Gaurav at Suyash Pet Clinic, Chembur. Even before we visited, he stayed in constant touch over the phone and guided us calmly. At the clinic, he immediately attended to Mylo, started him on saline, and did another X-ray. He clearly explained the situation, the size of the bone, the endoscopy procedure, and all associated risks, while also reassuring us throughout.

What truly stood out was his patience, kindness, and genuine care—not just for Mylo, but for us as anxious pet parents. He did everything he could to avoid surgery, and thankfully, the endoscopy was successful. Mylo recovered well, and we couldn’t be more grateful.

We had visited another hospital before this and felt very unsure due to their lack of clarity and significantly higher costs. In such emergencies, having a doctor who is both skilled and empathetic is truly a blessing.

Highly recommend Suyash Pet Clinic and Dr. Gaurav without hesitation. Writing this review after 2+ months, with a happy and healthy Mylo ❤️

featured_reviews.review_text:
We trusted this clinic with our 2-year-old cat during the most critical time of his life, and today we are left with heartbreak, trauma, and serious doubts about the care he received.

Our cat was already battling pleural effusion/FIP-related illness, but after the second drainage procedure done at this clinic, his condition worsened dramatically. Unlike the first drainage done elsewhere after which he breathed better and stabilized this time he developed pneumothorax and his breathing never improved afterward.

We were never properly prepared for how unstable his condition had become post-procedure. We also specifically informed the staff that our cat became extremely frightened and aggressive when touched without us present, and requested that he not be unnecessarily handled while we briefly stepped out. Despite that, he was taken out and handled. When we returned, we were met with his lifeless body.

Maybe no one can say with certainty what would have changed the outcome. But as pet parents who watched the drastic difference between the first and second procedures, we cannot ignore the feeling that mistakes, inadequate handling, or complications during treatment may have contributed to his final deterioration.

Losing a pet is devastating enough. Being left with unanswered questions and guilt afterward makes it even harder.

featured_reviews.name: NIKITA AMAR JHA
featured_reviews.review_text:
My friend and I lost our baby cat due to mycoplasma felis, thanks to her ignorance or apathy that lead to her giving us incorrect and apathetic advice. Our cat, TinTin was a stray and we did the first mistake of taking him to get vaccinated at Dr Prachi’s and the first red flag we noticed in her clinic was her offering dog food to the cat who could barely chew at it. A doctor who charges extravagantly cannot buy two separate bags of dog and cat food? This might seem like a little thing but it is not, because it demonstrates her inconsideration and carelessness, which was soon to resurface in a v serious form. Further our cat which was clearly emaciated was declared to be of healthy weight by her that day. Had she alerted us about his frailness (which is her literal job as a doctor), we could have done something. Our cat came back, and we noticed his reducing appetite day by day. So when my friend took the cat to her right after he skipped a meal, she ran some tests said the situation is critical but at the same time prescribed oral medications and liver sensitive food to him and said vaguely that he will get better in a week and fully better in three weeks. That day was one of the worst days in our baby’s life. He pooped continuously to the point when even blood came out and he suffered from severe diarrhoea. When Dr Prachi was informed of this in a state of panic, she prescribed an antibiotic and asked us to take him to Vetic if there is an emergency. The fact of the matter is that it was an emergency at that time but since she did not take the situation seriously, she made us put our guards down. The next morning, our baby was slowly breathing in the morning and was limp, we rushed to Vetic and met Dr Teja (who is a gem of a person; tried to save Tinu but couldn’t). He put him on IV medication and told us how ORAL MEDICATIONS HAD RUINED his condition and we should never given oral medications in this condition. He suffered from gastritis and internal bleeding. After successive days of continuous IV medication, he even started to get better and started becoming responsive. But since a lot of damage was already done to the baby’s body by the poor diagnosis and treatment done by Dr Prachi, his lungs collapsed on the morning of 30th March. Tinu passed away.
If this doctor is not an expert, she could have let us know earlier. And we would have taken our cat to another doctor. But she didn’t do that. Her carelessness costed our baby his life. Would ask her to introspect the consequences of her actions.
